items.title: Email Campaign · : Annual Service (1-Year Post-Install)
items.preview:
**Audience:** 23 contacts | 1-year anniversary trigger
**Send:** Tuesday, 10:00 AM ET
### Subject Lines
**Primary:** `It's been a year. Time for your 15-minute checkup.`
**Alternates:**
1. `Your annual service window just opened`
2. `One year down. Here's what happens next.`
3. `15 minutes keeps 10 years running`
4. `Annual service: the thing nobody skips twice`
### Preview Text
`Your FerroMax / Sovereign / system hit the 1-year mark. We come to you, 15-min service, then gone.`
---
### Email Body
**Subject:** It's been a year. Time for your 15-minute checkup.
{{FIRST_NAME}},
Your {{SYSTEM_NAME}} just hit the one-year mark.
That means it's time for the only service call most clients ever need: the annual checkup.
**What happens:**
We come to you. Check pressure, swap any consumables that need it, verify everything is dialed in. 15 minutes, then we're gone.
**Why it matters:**
ClearWave systems are engineered to run 10+ years. But that decade starts with year one. If something drifted (pressure, flow, a seal), we catch it now while it's easy.
Most clients who skip this end up calling us in year three with a problem that could have been prevented in year one.
**Your install date:** {{INSTALL_DATE}}
**Your system:** {{SYSTEM_NAME}}
**Service window:** Now through {{INSTALL_DATE + 60 days}}
[Book your annual service here →]
Takes 90 seconds to schedule. We handle the rest.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave
P.S. If you know someone fighting their water (sulfur, iron, hard water, chlorine taste), send them my way. Closed referrals pay **$500 cash** for referrals 1-5 this year, **$750** for 6-9, **$1,000** for 10+. Even if they just book a consult and don't close, you get a **$50 gift card**. [Send a referral here →]
---
### Performance Forecast
- **Expected open:** 38-44% (triggered, high-relevance, known sender)
- **Expected click:** 8-12% (single clear CTA, time-bounded urgency)
- **Expected conversion:** 35-50% of clicks → booked service (low friction, expected maintenance, trusted relationship)
### Source Justification
- **IDEA_SOURCING.md → Jobber lifecycle triggers:** "1-year service reminder... high intent, expected touch, clear next step"
- **Hard Rule #1 enforcement:** This is the FIRST time these clients are eligible for any service pitch
- **Voice:** Killing Bad Water Sales tone applied to internal confidence ("the thing nobody skips twice"), luxury product register applied to system naming and value framing
---

items.title: Email Campaign · : Referral Push (30-60 Days Post-Install)
items.preview:
**Audience:** 26 contacts | satisfied, honeymoon phase
**Send:** Thursday, 9:00 AM ET
### Subject Lines
**Primary:** `Quick favor (pays $500 if you know the right person)`
**Alternates:**
1. `The easiest $500 you'll make this month`
2. `Who else in your life is fighting their water?`
3. `Your referral bonus just unlocked`
4. `I'll pay you $500 to introduce me`
### Preview Text
`You've had your Sovereign / system for a month. If it's working, I have one ask: who else needs this?`
---
### Email Body
**Subject:** Quick favor (pays $500 if you know the right person)
{{FIRST_NAME}},
You've had your {{SYSTEM_NAME}} for about a month now.
If the water is better, the coffee tastes different, the soap actually rinses, I have one ask:
**Who else do you know who's fighting their water?**
Could be a neighbor with rust stains. A family member who buys bottled water by the pallet. A friend in a new build who thinks county water is "fine" until they taste yours.
**Here's what happens when you send someone my way:**
- They book a consult: you get a **$50 gift card** (even if they don't buy)
- They close: you get **$500 cash** (referrals 1-5 this year)
- Referrals 6-9: **$750**
- Referrals 10+: **$1,000**
Resets every January. No cap.
[Send a referral here →]
Takes 30 seconds. I'll take it from there. They get a free water assessment, you get paid, and someone you care about stops drinking garbage.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave
P.S. If you want to record a 60-second video testimonial instead (phone camera is fine), I'll send you a thank-you gift. Just hit reply and I'll send you the two questions to answer.
---
### Performance Forecast
- **Expected open:** 40-46% (recent relationship, curiosity + money hook)
- **Expected click:** 6-10% (transactional clarity, low effort, high reward)
- **Expected conversion:** 15-25% of clicks → referral submitted (requires them to know someone + take action, but zero financial risk, high reward)
### Source Justification
- **IDEA_SOURCING.md → Jobber lifecycle triggers:** "30-60d post-install referral ask... peak satisfaction, system is proven in their home, social proof instinct is high"
- **Hard Rule #3:** Explicitly pushes REFERRALS (with exact bonus structure), not reviews
- **Voice:** Killing Bad Water Sales directness ("I have one ask", "you get paid") + luxury product register system naming + conversational ask structure from analyzed corpus
---
## Why These Two
1. **Annual service (23 contacts):** Contractual expectation, zero sales friction, revenue-positive, prevents future service calls. This is the highest-conversion trigger in the Jobber lifecycle. If we don't email them, we're leaving $150-250/job on the table AND creating future problems.
2. **Referral push (26 contacts):** Honeymoon phase, intrinsic motivation to share, clear economic incentive. Recent Mailchimp campaigns show 0.00-0.01% click because they're cold-audience educational content. This is warm-audience transactional. Different game.
**Why NOT the other lists this week:**
- **RO replacement (25 contacts):** Lower urgency, harder to self-diagnose need, requires more education. Better as a drip sequence than a one-shot blast.
- **Concierge upsell (100 contacts):** Larger list, but colder intent. Needs a multi-touch sequence (education → math → objection handling → offer). Single email will underperform.
- **Cold leads (1,000 contacts):** High volume, low intent. Better as a re-engagement sequence (3-email arc) than a single shot. Also risks list health if we blast cold contacts without a value-first warm-up.
These two campaigns target **high-intent, time-bounded triggers** with **clear next steps** and **established trust**. That's the recipe for >5% click and >20% conversion.

---
